requirement:
When replacing results for an unfiltered workspace invocation or a filtered
invocation selecting at least one test, a prepared build configuration
incompatible with the active configuration under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` clears the whole
current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test
execution.

Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that
configuration is selected again. A filtered invocation selecting no tests
leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`.
rationale:
The three marked tests cover every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration_reset`. I read `Store::replace` (`src/execution_coverage/store.rs#impl[Store]/fn[replace]`) only to check how the fixtures drive it. I derived the expected behavior from the requirement text.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

1. **A filtered invocation that selects at least one test and has an incompatible configuration clears the whole set and activates the new configuration in one replacement.**
   - `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[incompatible_builds_reset_every_test_but_empty_focused_runs_do_not]` first stores two tests under configuration "a" and completes one with measurements.
   - It then runs a filtered replacement under "b" selecting only `a`. It asserts that the active configuration is "b" and that exactly one test remains.
   - The remaining test has no measurements. The other previous test, `b`, is gone, so the whole set was cleared and not only the selected identities.

2. **An unfiltered invocation with an incompatible configuration clears the set and activates the new configuration.**
   - The same test stores two completed tests under "a" and then runs an unfiltered replacement under "b" selecting one test.
   - It asserts configuration "b", a single `a` test, outcome "pending" and no measurements.

3. **Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that configuration is selected again.**
   - After switching to "b", the test switches back to "a" with a filtered selection of `b`.
   - It asserts that exactly one test remains, named `b`, and that it has no measurements. The earlier "a" results are not restored.

4. **A filtered invocation that selects no tests leaves the results and active configuration unchanged.**
   - The test runs an empty filtered replacement under an incompatible configuration "b". It asserts that `replace` returns false.
   - It then calls `record_empty` and asserts that configuration "a" is still active, both tests are still present, and measurements are still present.
   - `latest` points to the empty invocation. That follows `storage.replace`'s invocation-recording behavior and does not contradict this requirement.

5. **The clear and the activation happen in the same atomic replacement, before test execution.**
   - `failed_atomic_replacement_preserves_results_configuration_and_invocation` in `src/execution_coverage/store.rs` injects a failing trigger on inserts into `tests`. It then attempts an unfiltered replacement under the incompatible configuration "b".
   - It asserts that an error is returned. It also asserts that configuration "a", the latest invocation, and the completed result with its measurements are all unchanged.
   - This shows the clear and the configuration switch roll back together.
   - `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[a_failed_replacement_commit_reports_the_error_without_launching_execution]` is the end-to-end check. It runs `habeas coverage` with a different feature set and a failing commit trigger.
   - It asserts that the command fails with the error message, that the sentinel `cargo` wrapper never starts nextest execution, and that the stored runs and attempts are unchanged. This establishes that replacement precedes execution.

**Not assessed here**

How build-configuration compatibility is determined is delegated to `requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`, which is cited. The tests drive the compatible/incompatible distinction through differing configuration identifiers, so the reset behavior is tested under that cited rule.

I found no gaps and no missing {test} markings. The tests are marked and their assertions enforce the specified outcomes.

text: :::{req} storage.configuration_reset
When replacing results for an unfiltered workspace invocation or a filtered
invocation selecting at least one test, a prepared build configuration
incompatible with the active configuration under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` clears the whole
current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test
execution.
Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that
configuration is selected again. A filtered invocation selecting no tests
leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`.
:::{req} storage.configuration
Each coverage record MUST identify the recorded toolchain, compilation target,
Cargo build profile, enabled features, and instrumentation-affecting compiler
settings. These settings MUST determine build-configuration compatibility for
the combined view. A nextest scheduling profile alone MUST NOT make otherwise
compatible build configurations incompatible.
:::{req} storage.replace
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:
- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
`habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.
Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.
A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.
If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
